text: This chapter is one continuous scenario across all six remaining lessons — a single DBA's manual routine, automated end to end using everything this course has covered. This lesson sets the scene.

Meet Meridian Outfitters: an outdoor-gear e-commerce retailer with one full-time DBA, Priya Nair. Today her routine is almost entirely manual — backups run by hand most nights, a 40-minute morning health check done by eyeball, and schema changes deployed from emailed scripts pasted straight into production.

Over the next five lessons you'll build MeridianDBAOps: real PowerShell automation for backups, health checks, and maintenance; a source-controlled CI/CD pipeline for schema changes; and monitoring tuned so Priya isn't paged for every transient blip.

Everything lives in one Git repository, meridian-dbaops — the database project, the pipeline definition, and the PowerShell automation suite, side by side, the same repo a real solo DBA would actually use.

Next up: building the actual automation suite — real dbatools scripts for backups, health checks, and index maintenance, applying Chapters 1 and 2's patterns directly to Meridian Outfitters' environment.
